conventions.convention: The spacetime is oriented and time-oriented affine Minkowski space with metric diag(-1,1,1,1), length coordinates x⁰=ct, and μ≥0. Wave numbers and μ have inverse-length units; SI energy is ℏcω.

The construction assumes Countable Choice. The species assignment, CAR representation and zero-particle vacuum are adopted physical model data, without empirical premises or a general spin-statistics conclusion.

Hilbert pairings are linear in the second variable; annihilation is conjugate-linear and creation is linear in its Hilbert-space argument. The conjugate negative-energy space makes Ψ(F) antilinear in F.

The spatial Fourier transform has phase exp(-ik·x) and no prefactor; the momentum-space Hilbert measure is d³k/(2π)³. The test map integrates W_D(t,k) times the spatial Fourier transform over the length-coordinate time variable.
The μ=0 branch is admitted. The projection values at k=0 are the supplier's complementary rank-two projections; this single Lebesgue-null point does not change the multiplication operators.
The covariance test action is τ_g F(x)=(S⁻¹)†F(Λ⁻¹(x-a)). Positive Fock energy uses U_trans(a⁰)=exp(ia⁰K_D), while SI evolution uses U_evol(t)=U_trans(-ct) and H_D^SI=ℏcK_D.
Fock sectors start at n=0. The even algebra is the norm closure of finite linear combinations of the identity and even-degree products of bounded smeared fields and their adjoints.

load_bearing.statement: For Schwartz spinor tests F, the adopted field on fermionic Fock space over H₊⊕conjugate(H₋) is Ψ(F)=c(P₊u_F)+c†(conjugate(P₋u_F)), with the exact test-map and CAR construction of lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality. It is bounded and antilinear in F; no pointwise field operator is defined.

Assume Countable Choice and the adopted Dirac branch specified by def-qft-free-dirac-model. The bounded smeared field satisfies the displayed CAR and tested Dirac equation, graded locality for compact spacelike-separated supports, and spin-lift covariance. On the n-particle sector, U₂π=(-1)ⁿI and U₄π=I. The vacuum is invariant and globally cyclic; the translation spectrum lies in the closed future cone, with the stated positive-mass gap and SI energy conversion.

concerns.concern: Fact [F3] attributes the definition of the conjugate Hilbert space to def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces. That supplier defines Schwartz spaces and Fock sectors but does not define the conjugate Hilbert space. The exact conjugate-space scalar multiplication and pairing instead appear in def-qft-dirac-projections, already cited in [F2]. The construction remains supported, but this attribution should be corrected.
